title: maya-chen-private-deploy-networking-incident-notes-2026-03-04
content:
Incident snapshot / purpose:
- Notes/scratchpad for the private deployment networking incident impacting customer X (canary customer) — services in customer VPC cannot reach controlplane.core.internal over VPC peering (443). Intermittent from some subnets, consistent from others.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-02 22:10 UTC: first alert - controlplane healthchecks failing for canary app in us-west-2 private VPC.
- 2026-03-02 22:25 UTC: triage -> DNS resolution for controlplane host succeeds from bastion, but connect fails from app subnet.
- 2026-03-03 01:00 UTC: escalated to networking + private-deploy owners.
- 2026-03-04 08:30 UTC: current state of debugging below.

Commands / observations / interpretation:
1) DNS: dig +short controlplane.core.internal @10.0.0.2 -> 10.250.5.12. Route53 private hosted zone resolving across peering.

2) traceroute -n 10.250.5.12 -> stops after transit hop; peering path won't show full traceroute (expected).

3) curl -v https://controlplane.core.internal:443 --connect-timeout 10
   -> Connected to 10.250.5.12 port 443, TLS handshake: SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, curl: (35) SSL_connect error. Socket open then EOF.

4) openssl s_client -connect 10.250.5.12:443 -servername controlplane.core.internal -debug
   -> CONNECTED, write:errno=104, no peer certificate, SSL handshake read 0 bytes. errno=104 = connection reset by peer. Indicates server closing connection.

5) tcpdump on app ENI: SYN from app -> immediate RST from 10.250.5.12. Suggests host actively resetting.

6) AWS checks: SGs show app egress tcp:443 allowed, controlplane ingress allows VPC CIDR tcp:443. NACLs permissive. Route tables have route to pcx-0def. VPC peering shows AllowDnsResolutionFromRemoteVpc=true. VPC attributes enableDnsSupport/Hostnames=true.

7) LB / backend: target group health shows unhealthy in some AZs. Controlplane app logs show "Rejected connection: SNI mismatch" in auth filter.

8) Hypothesis on TLS/SNI: controlplane requires SNI matching controlplane.core.internal; sidecar (envoy) in some pods not setting SNI or sending IP as SNI -> server rejects with RST.

9) Envoy sidecar evidence: pods that succeed have envoy setting server_name; failing pods had older sidecar image (1.14) that did not set SNI. New image 1.16 fixes SNI behavior.

Actions tried and results:
- Redeployed envoy sidecar with explicit server_name in canary pod -> curl and openssl handshake succeed from that pod.
- Rolled sidecar injection template change to 3 nodes in us-west-2a (canary nodegroup) -> healthchecks recovered for those pods.

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Sidecar not forwarding SNI / wrong SNI -> server rejects (highest).
B) ALB/NLB TLS listener mismatch/termination mode causing early RST (possible).
C) SG/NACL/route issues causing RSTs (less likely after checks).
D) DNS peering misconfig (low, DNS resolved).
E) Node-level conntrack/ephemeral exhaustion (possible for subset of nodes).

Next steps / owners:
- Samir: roll sidecar injection template change to all nodegroups in cluster (high priority). JIRA NET-887.
- Noah: audit per-AZ sidecar versions across clusters; produce list of clusters with outdated image.
- Leah: review ALB listener TLS config and document expected behavior when SNI absent (CONFLUENCE-ENG-1234).
- Maya: add server-side logging to emit client SNI and source ip for handshake failures.
- Infra: add synthetic TLS checks (with and without SNI) in deploy pipeline.

Artifacts collected:
- tcpdump pcap: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2026-03-04/maya/tcpdump-app-eth0.pcap
- envoy configs from failing and fixed pods (internal repo link in JIRA).
- controlplane logs showing 'Rejected connection: SNI mismatch' (attached to JIRA).

Open questions:
- Why were some nodegroups still injecting old sidecar image? CI/upgrade pipeline gap?
- Do ALB types differ in behavior (RST vs TLS alert) on absent/wrong SNI?

Rollback plan if regression:
- Revert sidecar injection rollout; route traffic to fixed nodegroups; or enable short compatibility mode on controlplane to accept missing SNI.

Quick triage checklist for future incidents:
1) DNS resolve
2) tcpdump to confirm RST vs drop
3) openssl s_client -servername to test handshake
4) check sidecar SNI behavior / envoy config
5) check LB listener and SG/NACLs

Slack/JIRA snippets used:
- "curl: (35) SSL_connect error" and openssl write:errno=104 -> RST. tcpdump shows immediate RST from server IP. controlplane logs: 'Rejected connection: SNI mismatch'.

-- maya
